evidence: Plaut. Aul. 4.10.60: nūllus est tam parvī pretiī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of great or little value, magnī, parvī pretiī; to be valued, prized, in pretiō esse (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: be worth much (little, more, so much)
terms.comment: To value something is to say in the genitive what it is worth: magnī aestimāre, magnī facere (Quint. 11.1.38), ūnius assis aestimāre, not to give a penny for (Catull. 5.3). With verbs of valuing the genitive is used throughout, and comedy adds floccī, naucī, “not a straw”; with verbs of buying and costing only tantī, quantī, plūris, minōris (see cost a lot).

terms.gloss: to value, put a price on
evidence: Cic. Dom. 44: domum ēmit prope dīmidiō cārius quam aestimābat (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. value, worth (Marco Polo, c. 1300)
terms.comment: In antiquity only in a glossary (Lewis & Short); the medieval word.

evidence: Cato Agr. 2.7: vēndat oleum, sī pretium habeat (Lewis & Short s.v. pretium)

phrases.latin: formīca et musca contendēbant ācriter quae plūris esset
phrases.english: the ant and the fly were arguing hotly which of them was worth more

phrases.latin: rūmōrēsque senum sevēriōrum omnēs ūnius aestimēmus assis
phrases.english: and let’s value all the gossip of grumpy old men at a single penny

phrases.latin: Dionȳsium semper equidem, ut scīs, dīlēxī, sed cotīdiē plūris faciō
phrases.english: I have always been fond of Dionysius, as you know, but I value him more every day

phrases.latin: Neque ego illum maneō, neque floccī faciō
phrases.english: I’m not waiting for him, and I don’t care a straw about him
